title: Acquisition transition with restricted trust and reversible separation

scope.description: Fictional Cedar acquires Orbit. Orbit's existing tenant remains the home identity authority during a 180-day transition. A separately administered transition resource tenant hosts one sanitized deal-room app for ten sponsored synthetic Orbit identities. This is not a claim that acquisitions always require extra tenants.
outOfScope: Automatic trust of acquired-device compliance/MFA claims
Broad directory synchronization or tenant-wide admin delegation
Actual service-side session revocation or live separation
assumptions: The fictional transaction owner explicitly requires the unassessed Orbit estate not to share Cedar production administration.
Orbit home authentication remains a declared dependency for guest collaboration; this is not T3 identity independence.
The sanitized app can enforce resource-side session denial in addition to tenant trust/assignment removal.
The transition has a named exit owner and expires after 180 days without renewed approval.

sourceFacts.fact: Cross-tenant patterns can support acquisition coexistence, but a guest/resource tenant still depends on the configured home authentication and trust paths.
sourceFacts.scopeLimit: A separate resource tenant is not proof of independent identity, and transaction frequency is not an isolation requirement.

requirements.text: Keep the unassessed Orbit environment outside Cedar production identity administration while discovery/remediation occurs; the existing Cedar production tenant cannot meet the explicitly required transition administration boundary.
acceptance: No Orbit identity or transition workload receives a Cedar tenant/admin role.
Separate transition administration and allow-listed application trust are documented.
unknowns: Actual discovery and privilege-path review not performed.

requirements.text: Allow exactly ten approved synthetic Orbit users into the deal-room reader role only; do not enable broad synchronization, blanket inbound trust, cross-tenant administration or automatic trust of source device/MFA claims.
acceptance: Named home issuer, target app, user cohort and reader action only.
Unlisted user, wrong issuer, another app and admin action all denied.
unknowns: Tenant/app enforcement and source-assurance claims remain unverified.

requirements.text: Each guest has a Cedar sponsor, a 30-day renewable assignment expiry and a verified home identifier; removal or sponsor expiry must cause effective target denial within 30 minutes, including resource sessions.
acceptance: Joiner/mover/leaver inventory and expiry are observable.
Disablement, assignment removal and app-session denial measured separately.
Residual already exported data is explicitly outside revocation.

requirements.text: At transaction exit, complete the approved separation within four hours: deny new and existing guest access, remove memberships/trust/grants/workload bindings, and verify no indirect privileged path remains.
acceptance: Before/after directed authority graph covers human, workload, consent, app session and data export paths.
Fresh and previously issued-session negative tests both deny.
A rollback or retained quarantine decision is independently approved.
unknowns: Only a local separation model is eligible to execute; live test remains blocked.

requirements.text: Share only sanitized deal documents; retain raw Orbit/Cedar identity telemetry in its approved source jurisdiction and exchange approved incident summaries.
acceptance: Cross-tenant SOC views do not grant unrestricted raw data export.
unknowns: Product-specific data, log connector and regional coverage unverified.

requirements.text: Transition recovery and separation authority must not depend on Orbit guest authentication; maintain separately controlled cloud-only emergency methods and external trusted configuration/relationship state.
acceptance: Target emergency administration and baseline retrieval work without source home IdP.
Restore required transition object/edge state and deny removed privileges.
unknowns: No authorized R1/R3 or real independent custody retrieval.

requirements.text: Deployment automation is environment-bound and cannot recreate guest assignments/trust, grant consent, rewrite the baseline or create tenant administrators after separation.
acceptance: Workload issuer/subject/audience and scoped app permission inventory.
Separation removes bindings and resource permission; forbidden recreation denies.
unknowns: Actual credential/trust and deployed-code privileges untested.

requirements.text: At day 180, close or explicitly reapprove the transition with funded identity/SOC/recovery owners; acquisition frequency and a maturity label alone cannot authorize permanent tenant sprawl.
acceptance: Dated exit decision, license/operations/retention/recovery cost assumptions and staffed rota.
No automatic renewal without separation and privilege-path evidence.
unknowns: Staffing, lifecycle cost and exit acceptance not evidenced.
